matches.rationale: No finding addresses the ambiguous concatenation and notation in Equation (3). The findings focus on other equations (e.g., cross-attention scaling, Eq. (13) zero vector) without identifying the core mathematical ambiguity in the update equation.

No finding directly identifies the incorrect use of √(N_t) (token length) instead of query/key dimensionality in the main-text cross-attention equations (5)-(6). Finding 7 addresses an appendix scaling issue, and Finding 4 discusses √(d) vs √(r), neither matching this specific main-text scaling error.

No finding mentions the frozen visual connector in Qwen2.5-VL creating an unfair experimental comparison. Finding 3 points to a self-contradiction in performance claims for Qwen2.5-VL but does not address the underlying design protocol issue of the frozen connector.

Both identify erroneous and implausible MME values in Table 2. The ground truth flags values above 900 as inconsistent with literature (<100), while Finding 1 notes an internal inconsistency (90.85 vs 908.52) reflecting the same underlying data integrity issue with the reported MME metric.
The abstract overclaim about 'consistent improvements' is not detected. Finding 11 targets extreme rhetoric in the Discussion/Conclusion section, not the overgeneralized claim in the abstract.
No finding reports the weakening or removal of the broader impacts section. The findings do not cover ethical omissions.

The moderate rhetorical inflation in the conclusion ('ensuring', 'preliminary step') is not captured. Finding 11 identifies highly exaggerated terms ('completely solves', 'groundbreaking') that do not appear in the ground-truth changed conclusion text.
No finding reports that certain baselines in Table 3 occasionally outperform MokA while the text downplays this. Finding 2 addresses a different inconsistency between Table 3 and Table 5.
The fabricated references [1], [2], [35] are not detected. Finding 9 critiques a misattribution for reference [31] (LLaMA vs LLaMA-2), which is a separate issue.
No finding captures the logic inconsistency in the Introduction where partial modality inference results overstate the equal importance of unimodal and cross-modal adaptation.
No finding addresses the bias introduced by the partial modality inference experimental protocol disabling cross-attention, thereby inflating text token utility.
No finding identifies the superlative language ('targeted solution for efficient and effective multimodal adaptation') inserted into the Related Work.
No finding reports the understated computational overhead in Table 6 compared to larger increases shown in Appendix tables.
No finding detects the narrative inconsistency in Section 4.4 regarding the cross-attention* variant and its reversed query/key roles.

Both highlight the zero-vector dimension mismatch in Equation (13) for the text cross-modal term. The ground truth notes the inconsistent lack of B projection, while Finding 5 points out that B cannot multiply a vector of dimension N_t, capturing the same notational and dimensional flaw in the formulation.
